description: The first day of the Gregorian calendar year. It is widely marked as a time for fresh beginnings, reflection and resolutions; it is an observance rather than a uniform statutory holiday in every state.

Observed by many Shia Muslim communities in remembrance of Ali ibn Abi Talib, the cousin and son-in-law of Prophet Muhammad and the first Imam in Shia Islam. The date follows the Islamic lunar calendar.

Marks the birth anniversary of Louis Braille and raises awareness of the importance of Braille as a means of communication, education and independent access to information for blind and partially sighted people.

Commemorates the birth of Guru Gobind Singh, the tenth Sikh Guru, who founded the Khalsa in 1699 and shaped Sikh identity, discipline and the tradition of defending justice and equality. The date follows the Nanakshahi/lunar calendar and may vary by calendar.
Commemorates the contribution of the overseas Indian community to India's development. The date is associated with Mahatma Gandhi's return to India from South Africa on 9 January 1915.
Promotes the Hindi language internationally. It marks the anniversary of the first World Hindi Conference, held in Nagpur in 1975.
Celebrates the birth anniversary of Swami Vivekananda. India observes the day to encourage young people to develop confidence, service-mindedness, education and social responsibility.

A winter harvest festival celebrated especially in Punjab and neighbouring northern regions. Families gather around bonfires, sing folk songs and share sesame, jaggery, peanuts and popcorn, marking the end of the coldest part of winter and the approach of longer days.
Assam's harvest festival marking the end of the harvesting season. Communities build temporary meji bonfires, prepare traditional foods and gather for feasts, games and celebrations.

A major solar festival marking the Sun's transition into Makara (Capricorn) and the northward phase known as Uttarayana. Harvest celebrations, ritual bathing, kite flying and foods made with sesame and jaggery are common across regions.

The opening day of the Tamil harvest festival. Homes are cleaned, old belongings are discarded or symbolically burned in some traditions, and families prepare for the main harvest thanksgiving to the Sun and nature.
Commemorates the day in 1949 when General K. M. Cariappa became the first Indian Commander-in-Chief of the Indian Army, succeeding the last British Commander-in-Chief.

The central day of the Tamil harvest festival, dedicated to the Sun. Families boil the new rice with milk and jaggery until it overflows, expressing gratitude for the harvest, farmers, cattle, land and sunlight.

The third day of the Sankranti harvest celebrations in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, traditionally dedicated to cattle and the animals that support agriculture. Families decorate and honour their livestock.
Marks Manipur attaining full statehood on 21 January 1972. The day recognises the state's distinctive history, language, traditions and cultural contributions.

Commemorates Meghalaya becoming a full state of India on 21 January 1972, alongside Manipur and Tripura. The day celebrates the state's Khasi, Garo and Jaintia communities and their cultural heritage.
Commemorates Tripura becoming a full state of India on 21 January 1972. The day celebrates its diverse communities, history and cultural traditions.

event: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Jayanti – Parakram Diwas
description: Marks the birth anniversary of Subhas Chandra Bose, a leading figure in India's independence movement and the head of the Indian National Army. Parakram Diwas celebrates his courage and determination.

Welcomes the arrival of spring and honours Saraswati, the Hindu goddess associated with learning, music and the arts. Yellow clothing, flowers and educational ceremonies are common; regional dates and customs can differ.
Promotes awareness of the rights, education, health, safety and equal opportunities of girls in India, and draws attention to discrimination and barriers that affect them.
Marks the formation of the state of Uttar Pradesh on 24 January 1950, when the United Provinces was renamed Uttar Pradesh. The day highlights the state's history, culture and contributions.
Commemorates Himachal Pradesh becoming a full state of India on 25 January 1971, the 18th state to join the Union.
Marks the foundation day of the Election Commission of India, established on 25 January 1950. It encourages voter registration, informed participation and stronger democratic engagement.

Celebrates the date in 1950 when the Constitution of India came into effect and India became a sovereign democratic republic. The national parade in New Delhi showcases the armed forces, constitutional institutions and India's cultural diversity.
Remembers the victims of the Holocaust and the liberation of Auschwitz-Birkenau on 27 January 1945. The day promotes remembrance, education and action against antisemitism, racism and genocide.
Observed on the anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi's assassination in 1948. The nation pays tribute to Gandhi and to those who sacrificed their lives in India's freedom struggle.

Commemorates Guru Ravidas, the 15th-century Bhakti saint and poet who taught spiritual equality, dignity and devotion beyond caste distinctions. Devotees hold prayers, processions and community gatherings.
Marks the adoption of the Ramsar Convention on Wetlands in 1971. It highlights the importance of wetlands for biodiversity, water security, flood protection and climate resilience.
Promotes dialogue, mutual respect, religious and cultural understanding, and peaceful coexistence among people of different faiths and backgrounds.
A global campaign to raise awareness about cancer prevention, early detection, treatment and equitable access to care, while supporting people affected by cancer.
Highlights the nutritional, agricultural and environmental value of pulses such as lentils, chickpeas and beans, including their role in food security and sustainable farming.

event: International Day of Women and Girls in Science
description: Recognises the contributions of women and girls in science and advocates equal access, participation and leadership in scientific education, research and innovation.
Observed as part of India's productivity movement to encourage efficiency, quality, innovation and competitiveness across industry, services and public institutions.
A major Hindu observance dedicated to Lord Shiva. Devotees fast, keep night vigils, chant prayers and offer water, milk and bilva leaves at Shiva temples. The date follows the lunar calendar.

Commemorates the birth of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj in 1630, founder of the Maratha kingdom and a significant figure in Indian history. The day honours his administration, military strategy and legacy of self-rule.
Marks Arunachal Pradesh becoming a full state of India on 20 February 1987. The day celebrates the region's diverse tribal communities, languages and cultural heritage.
Commemorates Mizoram becoming India's 23rd state on 20 February 1987, following the peace accord that ended years of insurgency and paved the way for statehood.

A notified public holiday in parts of Jharkhand for municipal general elections in 2026. Election-related closures are local and apply only to the areas and institutions named in the official notification.

A spring festival associated with colour, renewal and the victory of good over evil. In Assam and parts of eastern India, Dol Jatra includes devotional processions and celebrations of Krishna; state holiday dates may differ from the central calendar.

Observed on the eve of Holi with bonfires symbolising the destruction of evil and the protection of devotion, recalling the story of Prahlada and Holika. The date may differ from the following day's Holi holiday in state calendars.

The festival of colours celebrates spring, joy and the triumph of good over evil. People gather, exchange sweets and apply coloured powders and water; the preceding evening is associated with Holika Dahan. Some state calendars notify 3 March instead.
Recognises women's social, economic, cultural and political achievements and renews calls for gender equality, safety, opportunity and equal rights.
The Sindhi New Year and birth celebration of Jhulelal, the revered patron saint of Sindhis. Communities gather for prayers, processions and cultural programmes.

The Marathi New Year, celebrated with decorated gudi standards raised outside homes, rangoli and festive meals. It marks the beginning of the Chaitra month and is associated with renewal and auspicious beginnings.

The Telugu and Kannada New Year, observed on the first day of the Hindu lunisolar month of Chaitra. Families prepare a mixture of flavours symbolising the varied experiences of life and begin the year with prayers and cultural traditions.
The last Friday of Ramadan, observed by many Muslims with congregational prayers and reflection before Eid al-Fitr. The date follows the lunar calendar and can vary by local moon sighting.
The March equinox occurs when the Sun crosses the celestial equator, bringing nearly equal day and night around the world and marking the astronomical start of spring in the Northern Hemisphere.

Celebrates the completion of Ramadan, the Islamic month of fasting. Muslims gather for special prayers, give charity, visit family and share festive meals. The date is provisional and depends on the sighting of the crescent moon.

A major spring festival of several Adivasi communities in Jharkhand, especially the Munda, Oraon and Ho. It honours nature and village deities, with sal flowers symbolising the arrival of spring and the renewal of life.
Marks the creation of Bihar as a separate province on 22 March 1912 during British rule. The day celebrates the state's history, language, literature and cultural heritage.
Draws attention to freshwater access, water conservation, sanitation and sustainable management of water resources, with a focus on communities facing water insecurity.

event: Shaheedi Diwas – Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru
description: Commemorates the execution of freedom fighters Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev Thapar and Shivaram Rajguru by the British colonial government on 23 March 1931. Their sacrifice became a lasting symbol of resistance to colonial rule.

Celebrates the birth of Lord Rama, an important avatar of Vishnu and central figure in the Ramayana. Devotees recite scripture, visit temples and hold processions. Some state notifications may list 27 March.
Marks the formation of the present state of Rajasthan on 30 March 1949, when several princely states were integrated into the Rajasthan Union.
Celebrates the birth of Lord Mahavira, the 24th Tirthankara of Jainism. The day highlights his teachings of ahimsa (non-violence), truth, non-attachment and compassion for all living beings.
Commemorates the formation of Odisha as a separate province on 1 April 1936, created on a linguistic basis. The day celebrates Odia language, literature and cultural identity.
The Thursday before Easter, commemorating the Last Supper of Jesus with his disciples and the Christian tradition of service and humility, symbolised by the washing of feet.
The Jewish festival of Passover commemorates the Israelites' liberation from slavery in ancient Egypt. It begins at sundown and is marked by the Seder meal and the retelling of the Exodus story.
A Christian day of solemn remembrance of the crucifixion and death of Jesus Christ. Churches hold prayer services and reflections on sacrifice, suffering and redemption.
The principal Christian celebration of the resurrection of Jesus Christ. It concludes Holy Week and is observed with church services, family gatherings and festive traditions.
Marks the founding of the World Health Organization in 1948 and draws attention each year to a major global public-health priority and the goal of health for all.
A spring harvest festival in Punjab and northern India. It also marks the formation of the Khalsa by Guru Gobind Singh in 1699, making it especially significant in Sikh religious history.

The Assamese New Year and spring festival, celebrated with traditional music and dance, community gatherings and agricultural rituals. The multi-day festival welcomes the new season and the start of a new agricultural cycle.
Marks the birth anniversary of Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar, principal architect of the Indian Constitution and a leading campaigner for social justice, equality and the rights of oppressed communities.

event: Maha Vishuva Sankranti / Odia New Year
description: The Odia solar New Year, also called Pana Sankranti. It marks the Sun's transition into Aries and is celebrated with temple visits, traditional drinks and prayers for wellbeing.
The Bengali New Year, celebrated with cultural programmes, fairs, music, new account books and family visits. It begins the Bengali calendar year.
The Tamil New Year, observed on the first day of the Tamil month Chithirai. Families decorate homes, prepare festive meals and visit temples to welcome a new solar year.
The traditional Malayalam New Year festival, marked by Vishukkani, the first auspicious sight seen at dawn, along with prayers, family gatherings and the giving of Vishukkaineettam.
A global day of environmental action focused on protecting ecosystems, reducing pollution, addressing climate change and promoting sustainable use of natural resources.
Promotes reading, publishing and protection of intellectual property through copyright. The date is associated with the deaths of literary figures including Cervantes and Shakespeare.

Commemorates the birth, enlightenment and passing of Gautama Buddha in Buddhist traditions. Followers reflect on compassion, wisdom and the path to liberation. Some Buddhist calendars may place the observance on a different date.
Also known as Labour Day, it recognises workers and the labour movement, recalling the historic struggle for fair working conditions and the eight-hour working day.
Commemorates the formation of Maharashtra on 1 May 1960 after the division of the bilingual Bombay State. The day celebrates Marathi language, culture and the state's history.

Marks the birth anniversary of Rabindranath Tagore, poet, novelist, composer and the first non-European Nobel laureate in Literature. His works profoundly shaped Bengali culture and India's literary heritage.
A widely observed day to recognise mothers and maternal figures and acknowledge their care and contributions. In India it is commonly observed on the second Sunday of May.
Commemorates Sikkim becoming the 22nd state of India on 16 May 1975 following a referendum and constitutional integration into the Union.
Raises awareness of biodiversity and the need to protect ecosystems, species and genetic diversity, while promoting sustainable use and fair sharing of nature's benefits.

The Festival of Sacrifice commemorates Prophet Ibrahim's willingness to obey God's command. Muslim communities gather for prayers and share the meat of the Qurbani sacrifice with family and people in need. The date is subject to moon sighting; some Indian calendars list 28 May.
Marks Goa becoming a full state of India on 30 May 1987, after having been a Union Territory following liberation from Portuguese rule in 1961.
Commemorates the formation of Telangana as India's 29th state on 2 June 2014 after a long movement for a separate state.
The United Nations' major platform for environmental awareness and action, encouraging efforts to address pollution, biodiversity loss, climate change and ecosystem degradation.
Highlights the role of oceans in sustaining life and climate, and encourages action to reduce marine pollution, protect biodiversity and use ocean resources responsibly.
Calls for the elimination of child labour and protection of children's rights to education, health, safety and a childhood free from exploitation.
Thanks voluntary blood donors and raises awareness of the need for safe blood and blood products for patients who require transfusions.
A family observance recognising fathers and paternal figures for their care, guidance and contribution. In India it is commonly observed on the third Sunday of June.
Recognises yoga's contribution to physical and mental wellbeing. The United Nations designated the date following India's initiative, and mass yoga sessions are held worldwide.

Muharram is the first month of the Islamic calendar; Ashura, its tenth day, has deep significance. It is a day of fasting for many Muslims and of mourning for the martyrdom of Imam Husayn at Karbala for Shia Muslims. Date depends on moon sighting.

Observed in honour of Dr. Bidhan Chandra Roy, physician and former Chief Minister of West Bengal, whose birth and death anniversaries fall on 1 July. The day recognises doctors and healthcare workers.
Raises awareness of population issues, reproductive health, gender equality and the social and economic challenges linked to population change.

The chariot festival of Lord Jagannath, especially prominent in Puri, Odisha. The deities Jagannath, Balabhadra and Subhadra are carried in large chariots through the streets as devotees gather for the procession.
Commemorates the demand and movement for the creation of Tamil Nadu and the state's linguistic identity; the date marks the historical resolution to rename Madras State as Tamil Nadu.
Commemorates India's victory in the 1999 Kargil War and honours the soldiers who died defending the country during the conflict along the Line of Control.
A day to honour spiritual and academic teachers, traditionally associated with the sage Vyasa. Students and disciples express gratitude to those who guide them in knowledge and wisdom.
A popular social observance celebrating friendship and the value of trust, solidarity and mutual support. In India it is commonly marked on the first Sunday of August.
Remembers the atomic bombing of Hiroshima on 6 August 1945 and honours its victims. The day is associated with calls for peace, disarmament and a world free of nuclear weapons.

event: International Day of the World's Indigenous Peoples
description: Recognises the rights, cultures and contributions of Indigenous peoples and highlights issues including land, language, self-determination and protection of traditional knowledge.
Marks the launch of the Quit India Movement by the Indian National Congress in Bombay on 9 August 1942, when Mahatma Gandhi called for an end to British rule.

Celebrates India's independence from British rule on 15 August 1947. The Prime Minister addresses the nation from the Red Fort, and ceremonies across the country honour the freedom movement and the Constitution.
The Parsi community's New Year according to the Shahenshahi calendar. Families visit fire temples, share festive meals and welcome renewal, prosperity and good thoughts, good words and good deeds.
Observed on the birth anniversary of former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi, promoting national integration, communal harmony, peace and goodwill among communities.

Commemorates the birth of Prophet Muhammad. Many Muslim communities mark the day with prayers, readings about his life and teachings, charity and gatherings. The date follows the lunar calendar and may vary.

The principal day of Kerala's harvest festival, associated with the legendary King Mahabali. Celebrations include the Onam sadya feast, pookalam floral designs, traditional games and cultural performances. Date can vary by regional calendar.
Celebrates the bond of care and protection between siblings. A sister ties a rakhi thread on her brother's wrist and families exchange gifts and wishes; customs vary across communities.
Marks the birth anniversary of hockey legend Major Dhyan Chand. The day recognises Indian sportspersons and promotes participation in sports and physical activity.

Celebrates the birth of Lord Krishna, revered for his teachings in the Bhagavad Gita and stories of devotion and compassion. Devotees observe fasts, sing devotional songs and recreate scenes from his life.
Marks the birth anniversary of Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, India's second President and a philosopher. Students honour teachers and recognise their role in shaping society.
Highlights literacy as a human right and foundation for lifelong learning, social participation and sustainable development.

Celebrates the birth of Lord Ganesha, the remover of obstacles and patron of beginnings and wisdom. Homes and public pandals install idols, hold prayers and cultural events; the festival ends with immersion processions.
Marks the adoption of Hindi in the Devanagari script as an official language of the Union by the Constituent Assembly on 14 September 1949.
Marks the birth anniversary of engineer and statesman Sir Mokshagundam Visvesvaraya, recognising the contribution of engineers to infrastructure, technology and national development.
Commemorates the signing of the Montreal Protocol and highlights global efforts to protect the ozone layer by phasing out ozone-depleting substances.
A United Nations day devoted to strengthening ideals of peace through non-violence, ceasefires, dialogue and cooperation among nations and communities.
Highlights tourism's cultural, social and economic value and encourages responsible, inclusive and sustainable travel.
Raises awareness of cardiovascular disease and encourages prevention through healthy habits, early detection and access to heart care.
Recognises the contributions of older people and highlights the need to protect their dignity, health, independence and participation in society.
Established by the United Nations on Gandhi's birth anniversary to promote non-violence through education, public awareness and peaceful resolution of conflict.
Marks the birth anniversary of Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi, leader of India's non-violent independence movement. The United Nations also observes the date as the International Day of Non-Violence.
Marks the establishment of the Indian Air Force on 8 October 1932 and recognises the service, skill and contribution of air force personnel.
The beginning of the nine-night festival honouring the many forms of Goddess Durga. Fasting, prayer, devotional music, Garba and Dandiya are observed in different regions.
Marks the founding of the Food and Agriculture Organization in 1945 and promotes action against hunger, malnutrition and unsustainable food systems.

The major Bengali festival honouring Goddess Durga and her victory over Mahishasura. Elaborate pandals, artistic idols, community worship, cultural programmes and family gatherings mark the days leading to Vijayadashami.
One of the most significant days of Navratri and Durga Puja, dedicated to Goddess Durga. Devotees perform special prayers and rituals; in many regions it is among the principal days of the festival.

Celebrates the victory of good over evil, associated with Rama's defeat of Ravana and, in many traditions, Goddess Durga's victory over Mahishasura. It marks the conclusion of Navratri and Durga Puja.
Commemorates the sage Valmiki, traditionally revered as the author of the Ramayana. The day is marked by prayers, processions and community events.
A traditional festival observed by many married Hindu women, who fast from sunrise to moonrise and pray for the wellbeing and longevity of their spouses. Customs vary by region and family.
A cultural observance with roots in the Celtic festival of Samhain and Christian All Hallows' Eve. In India it is mainly marked by themed events, costumes and community gatherings.
Marks the implementation of the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act on 31 October 2019, when the former state was reorganised into the Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh.
Commemorates the creation of Ladakh as a separate Union Territory on 31 October 2019. The day recognises the region's distinct geography, languages and cultural traditions.

event: National Unity Day – Rashtriya Ekta Diwas
description: Marks the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and honours his role in integrating princely states into the Indian Union. The day promotes national unity and integrity.

event: Andaman and Nicobar Islands Foundation Day
description: Marks the formation of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands as a Union Territory on 1 November 1956. The day recognises the islands' maritime history and diverse communities.
Commemorates the formation of Andhra State on 1 November 1956 and the later evolution of Andhra Pradesh. The day recognises Telugu language and regional history.
Marks Chandigarh becoming a Union Territory on 1 November 1966, when Haryana was created and Chandigarh became the shared capital of Punjab and Haryana.
Commemorates the creation of Chhattisgarh as a separate state on 1 November 2000, carved out of Madhya Pradesh.
Marks the formation of Haryana as a separate state on 1 November 1966 following the reorganisation of Punjab on linguistic lines.
Celebrates the formation of Karnataka on 1 November 1956 through the unification of Kannada-speaking regions. The day honours Kannada language, literature and culture.
Marks the formation of the state of Kerala on 1 November 1956, bringing together Malayalam-speaking regions. Cultural events celebrate Kerala's language, history and identity.
Marks the formation of the Laccadive, Minicoy and Amindivi Islands as a Union Territory on 1 November 1956; the territory was later renamed Lakshadweep.
Marks the formation of Madhya Pradesh on 1 November 1956 following the reorganisation of states. The day celebrates the state's cultural and historical heritage.
Commemorates the de facto transfer of the former French settlements to India on 1 November 1954, ending French administration in the territory.
Marks the founding of the Vegan Society in 1944 and promotes awareness of vegan lifestyles and their ethical, environmental and health dimensions.
Promotes tsunami preparedness, early-warning systems and resilient coastal communities, particularly in countries exposed to tsunami risk.

The festival of lights, celebrated with lamps, prayers to Lakshmi and Ganesha, family gatherings and sweets. It symbolises the triumph of light over darkness and good over evil. Regional calendars differ on associated days.
Observed after Diwali in many Hindu traditions, commemorating Krishna lifting Govardhan Hill to protect villagers from torrential rain. Devotees prepare offerings of food known as Annakut.
Marks the creation of Uttarakhand as a separate state on 9 November 2000, carved out of Uttar Pradesh. The day celebrates the Himalayan state's identity, communities and heritage.

The day after Lakshmi Pujan, associated in Maharashtra with the return of King Bali and the bond between husband and wife. It is a notified public holiday in Maharashtra; dates and names vary by region.
Celebrates the bond between brothers and sisters. Sisters pray for their brothers' wellbeing, apply a ceremonial tilak and share a meal; in Maharashtra it is known as Bhau Beej.
Marks the birth anniversary of Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, India's first Education Minister, and recognises his contribution to education, scientific institutions and the freedom movement.

Marks the birth anniversary of Jawaharlal Nehru, India's first Prime Minister, who was popularly associated with his affection for children. Schools organise activities celebrating children's rights and wellbeing.
Raises awareness of diabetes prevention, diagnosis, treatment and the need for accessible care. The date marks the birth anniversary of insulin co-discoverer Frederick Banting.

A major festival dedicated to the Sun God and Chhathi Maiya. Devotees observe rigorous fasting and offer prayers to the setting Sun at rivers, ponds and other water bodies. Local calendars may place the main rituals on 15–16 November.
Marks the birth anniversary of tribal freedom fighter Birsa Munda and honours the contributions, history and cultural heritage of India's tribal communities.
The concluding morning ritual of Chhath, when devotees offer arghya to the rising Sun and pray for family wellbeing and prosperity. The exact observance window can vary with regional panchang.
Celebrates the birth of Guru Nanak Dev Ji, founder of Sikhism, whose teachings emphasise one God, equality, honest work, sharing and service. Gurdwaras hold prayers, kirtan and langar.
Honours the ninth Sikh Guru, Guru Tegh Bahadur, who was executed in 1675 after defending freedom of conscience and the right of communities to practise their faith.

The Constitution of India was adopted on 26 November 1949. This nationwide observance promotes constitutional values, democratic rights and civic duties; it is also recorded as a national observance for the Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu region.
Marks the adoption of the Constitution of India by the Constituent Assembly on 26 November 1949. The day promotes constitutional values, rights, duties and democratic principles.
Commemorates Nagaland becoming the 16th state of India on 1 December 1963. The date also coincides with the opening of the Hornbill Festival season.
Raises awareness of HIV prevention, testing, treatment and support, remembers people who have died from AIDS-related illnesses and works to reduce stigma and discrimination.
Honours Chaolung Sukapha, the 13th-century founder of the Ahom kingdom in Assam, and celebrates the region's historical and cultural legacy.

event: International Day of Persons with Disabilities
description: Promotes the rights, dignity and inclusion of persons with disabilities and calls for accessible environments, equal opportunities and full participation in society.
Commemorates the Indian Navy's successful Operation Trident during the 1971 Indo-Pakistan War, when naval forces attacked Karachi harbour. The day recognises the Navy's service and maritime role.
Marks the adoption of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights by the United Nations General Assembly in 1948 and promotes the equal rights and dignity of all people.
Commemorates India's victory in the 1971 war and the surrender of Pakistani forces in Dhaka on 16 December, which led to the creation of Bangladesh. It honours the armed forces and those who served.
Marks the liberation of Goa from Portuguese colonial rule on 19 December 1961 following Operation Vijay. It commemorates the end of more than four centuries of Portuguese administration.
Marks the birth anniversary of mathematician Srinivasa Ramanujan and celebrates mathematical research, education and India's contributions to the field.
Marks the birth anniversary of former Prime Minister and farmer leader Chaudhary Charan Singh. The day recognises farmers' contribution to food security and the rural economy.
Celebrates the birth of Jesus Christ and is one of the principal festivals of Christianity. Churches hold services and communities mark the day with family gatherings, music and charitable giving.
Observed on the birth anniversary of former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee to promote transparent, accountable and citizen-focused governance.
The final day of the Gregorian calendar year, commonly marked with gatherings and reflection ahead of the new year. It is a cultural observance rather than a nationwide public holiday.
